title: 001 — The machines were never the whole story.
summary: From Smith’s pin factory to AI: a visual exploration of automation, economics, and who gets the gains. Includes historical perspectives, charts, an interactive productivity experiment, and sourced explorations of Newton, cognitive offloading, meaningful work, and the freedom to pursue new questions. Includes a companion video with James Suzman.

title: Groundwork: the research behind the questions
summary: Explore my research journey through environmental microbiology, soil health, and sustainable farming systems.

title: Building: ideas taking shape
summary: A collection of agricultural tools, apps, and experiments connecting research to everyday decisions.

title: Screen Time: stories worth talking about
summary: Browse 23 personal takes on movies, series, and animation, with ratings and a searchable collection.

title: On the Bookshelf: soil, community, and work
summary: Reading notes on The Farm Is Here by Jeff Tkach, plus James Suzman’s Work and his talk on how work has shaped society.

title: On the Bookshelf: How to Feed the World
summary: Added to Bookshelf: my April 10, 2025 review of Vaclav Smil’s How to Feed the World. Reading from within organic agriculture, I explore nutrients, energy, scale, and the overlooked costs behind food-system solutions. Includes the original Medium review and a connection to The Pathology of More.

title: 002 — God is for the poor.
summary: A long-form story about faith as hope under financial insecurity, religious belonging as a language of public trust, and the responsibility that follows. Includes two sourced survey graphs, conceptual illustrations, and examples of faith organizing practical care and demands for rights.

title: Groundwork: the Farming Systems Trial, read five ways
summary: One field since 1981, three ways to farm it. Five papers from the Farming Systems Trial at Rodale Institute on soil carbon, emissions, grain nutrition, and farm economics, with two sourced figures and the patterns that connect them to my soil health benchmarking work.
